question.text: Two rods $A$ and $B$ of identical dimensions are at temperature $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. If $\mathrm{A}$ is heated upto $180^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ upto $\mathrm{T}^{\circ} \mathrm{C},$ then the new lengths are the same. If the ratio of the coefficients of linear expansion of $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ is $4: 3,$ then the value of $T$ is

solution.text:
Change in length in both rods are same i.e.

$\Delta \ell_{1}=\Delta \ell_{2}$

$\ell \alpha_{1} \Delta \theta_{1}=\ell \alpha_{2} \Delta \theta_{2}$

$\begin{array}{l}

\frac{\alpha_{1}}{\alpha_{2}}=\frac{\Delta \theta_{2}}{\Delta \theta_{1}} \quad\left[\because \frac{\alpha_{1}}{\alpha_{2}}=\frac{4}{3}\right] \\

\frac{4}{3}=\frac{\theta-30}{180-30}

\end{array}$

$\theta=230^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
